one_month_reasoning: No company earnings fall in the window. The company has not announced its Q1 FY27 date (no 8-K or release; Earnings Whispers' 'confirmed' is a third-party label). Past fiscal-Q1 releases came on Nov 2, 2023, Nov 7, 2024 and Nov 4, 2025, so the print is expected around Nov 3-6, after the horizon. Nov 1 is a Sunday, so the effective mark is the Oct 30 close. Inside the window: hyperscaler Q3 results and 2027 capex commentary in the last week of October, which move the optics group together, and a likely mid-October date announcement. On the other side, the stock just ran ~20% in four sessions to a new high, and 10b5-1 insider sales are near-daily (CFO sold at $1,048.50 on Oct 1). Reversal after the sharp move roughly offsets momentum and capex-season tailwinds, so I stay near-neutral: median ~$1,080, monthly log-sigma ~0.25 (annual vol/3.5 = 0.28), P(>=spot) ~0.49. This is unchanged from round 1. Only the date's status changed, and either way it falls outside the window.

fair_value.method: Blend of P/E (NTM EPS at Oct-2027 ~$36 x 30x + $10.7 net cash = $1,091, w 0.5), EV/EBITDA (~$4.4B NTM EBITDA x 22x + $1.1B net cash / 103M = $950, w 0.3) and EV/sales (~$10.0B x 9x = $884, w 0.2). Fair value ~$1,007, ~7% below the $1,085 close. Every multiple sits at or below the median-equivalent of an 11-company AI-optics/connectivity peer set.

bear.story: AI optics digestion: 2027 hyperscaler capex growth disappoints, industry InP/EML capacity (COHR, AVGO, Japanese and Chinese entrants) closes the 30%+ supply gap, and pricing and the 50% gross margin reset. Customer A/B (42% of revenue) push out orders. FY28 EPS lands ~$24 against $33-35 consensus, and the market pays ~20x trough-like multiples.

base.story: Execution continues: Q1 FY27 guide met (~$1.25B / $4.20), OCS and 1.6T/200G EML ramp, CPO laser shipments start 2H CY27; FY28 EPS tracks the ~$33-35 consensus and NTM EPS at the horizon is ~$36. The multiple compresses from ~42x NTM today to ~30x as growth slows toward 15-25%, leaving the stock roughly flat.

bull.story: The CEO's ~$40 2028 earnings power proves conservative: scale-up CPO and external light source orders broaden beyond the lead customer, NTM EPS at the horizon is ~$42-45, and the market keeps a ~42-45x multiple (top third of peers, like ANET/MRVL today) on InP scarcity.

thesis_break_reason: $600 is ~18x current FY28 consensus EPS (~$33, MarketBeat), below every peer's next-FY P/E except AVGO (18.3x) and under the 25.1x peer median. The market would pay that only if it had concluded FY28 earnings will undershoot consensus by 25%+ or that they are a cyclical peak. Plausible causes: lead-customer push-outs, 2027 hyperscaler capex cuts, a CPO architecture shift away from Lumentum lasers, or a guide-down at the ~Nov 3-6 or Feb print. A ~45% drawdown is also beyond what one year of ordinary noise at a ~0.65 forward sigma would usually produce against a strongly rising earnings path.

reasoning: Round-2 revision. The supervisor showed my $26.40 FY28 consensus was stale. I re-checked it: MarketBeat (updated 2026-10-03) gives $19.78 FY27 -> $32.96 FY28, and StockAnalysis gives $21.78 -> $34.73 [14,16]. My $28 base was therefore 15-20% too low. I now use NTM EPS at the horizon of ~$36. I also adopt the supervisor's net cash (~$1.10B, $10.7/sh) and 103M diluted shares, and I accept that the '$1.6B current converts' are mainly 2032 notes with cash-settled principal, so convert dilution is no longer a separate catalyst. I accept that Nov 5 is not company-confirmed. New in-lane alt data was thin: open US roles were few (9 in July, mostly fab/process engineering [18]), while the company-announced Greensboro InP fab (400+ jobs [17]) confirms capacity build-out, which supports volume but also signals that the industry InP supply gap will narrow. That is why I keep the bear case at 25%. Comps: 11 listed AI-optics/connectivity peers (StockAnalysis, 2026-10-02 close). Medians are 37.7x current-FY P/E, 25.1x next-FY P/E and 10.8x forward sales. LITE's growth is at the median and its margins are above most, but it is more cyclical and concentrated. I therefore give no premium: 30x NTM P/E, 22x non-GAAP EV/EBITDA and 9x EV/sales, all inside the peer ranges. Blended fair value is ~$1,007 (from $980). Base rates: realized vol 97%; I use a ~0.66 forward log-sigma around a ~$1,060 median, between fair value and spot to give some credit to the earnings momentum, and slightly fatten the left tail. This gives P(>=$1,085) ~0.49. Scenario mean ~$1,150 (25% $500 / 50% $1,100 / 25% $1,900). Research limits: Twelve Data statistics required a paid plan, X and Reddit were not reachable, and no prediction market exists on LITE. Option data was deliberately not used.

comps_summary.lite_today: LITE at $1,085.42: fwd P/E 49.8x FY27 consensus $21.78 and 31.3x FY28 $34.73 (StockAnalysis; MarketBeat has $19.78/$32.96); EV $96.3B = ~22.6x FY28 non-GAAP-style EBITDA ($9.68B x ~44%) but 37.4x on the same GAAP-margin proxy used for peers; consensus revenue +53%, EPS +60% next FY - i.e. at the peer median on growth.
comps_summary.where_my_multiples_sit: P/E leg: 30x NTM EPS at the Oct-2027 horizon. That is below the peer current-FY forward median (37.7x) and above the next-FY median (25.1x), inside both ranges. Because a multiple applied a year out sits on EPS 1.5-2 fiscal years ahead of today's, the relevant comparator lies between those two medians (~30x), so I treat 30x as roughly peer-median, not a premium. EV/EBITDA leg: 22x NTM non-GAAP EBITDA. The peer proxy is GAAP-margin based. On that proxy LITE itself screens at 37.4x next-FY versus ~22.6x on non-GAAP-style EBITDA (ratio ~0.6), and the same ratio applied to the 32.6x peer next-FY median gives ~20x. So 22x is at or just above median-equivalent and inside the range. EV/sales leg: 9x NTM sales, below the 10.8x peer forward median and inside the 1.6-23.2x range. At LITE's ~44% EBITDA margin, 9x sales is consistent with ~20x EBITDA.
comps_summary.justification: I do not claim a persistent premium. LITE's growth next FY (+53% revenue, +60% EPS) is at the peer median, not above it, so growth does not earn a premium. Its margin is structurally high for a component maker: guided Q1 FY27 op margin is 39.5-40.5%, against StockAnalysis TTM EBITDA margins of ~11-20% at FN, CLS, CIEN and COHR, though AVGO (~59%) and ANET (~44%) are higher. That supports a premium to the assemblers. Cyclicality cuts the other way, and I judge it persistent through the horizon. LITE sells InP lasers and modules whose 50% gross margin rests on a supply gap that COHR, AVGO and Chinese entrants are adding capacity to close. Two customers were 42% of FY26 revenue. The predecessor JDSU went through a full boom-bust. Systems vendors and diversified semis (ANET, AVGO, MRVL) carry recurring or platform revenue that LITE lacks. The balance sheet is neutral to slightly positive: ~$1.1B net cash, versus net debt at COHR, CIEN, MRVL, AVGO and CLS. Netting margin (+) against cyclicality and concentration (-), I set each multiple at or slightly below the median-equivalent rather than at a premium. Sell-side outperformance calls were not used.
